name: convertToEm
summary: Converts an absolute length to em, against the font size it will be read in.

arguments.name: $value
accepts: an absolute length: px, pt, pc, in, cm, mm or q
a relative one such as rem, em, ch or vw is refused, since it has no fixed size

arguments.name: $base
accepts: the font size the result is read in, 16px by default
an absolute length, and not zero

caveats: Until 4.0.0 the unit was added as text, so the function returned the string `1.5em` rather than a number: it printed the same, and `convertToEm(24px) * 2` stopped the build with Sass's "Undefined operation". It now returns a number, as `remify` always has.

`em` is relative to the element's own font size, and that is the whole difference between it and `rem`. Until 4.0.0 the 16px base could not be changed, so inside `.card { font-size: 14px }` a `padding: convertToEm(24px)` was 21px on the page and nothing said so. Pass `$base` to say what the result is read in.

Any absolute length converts, not only pixels: Sass reduces `pt`, `pc`, `in`, `cm`, `mm` and `q` to the same scale, so `convertToEm(24pt)` is the same as `convertToEm(32px)`. All six used to be refused although each has one right answer. The relative units stay refused, because they have none.
